answer: A dawn watchtower keeps an agent economy honest when every identity must hand-copy its own chronicle page there at first light, one quill in one hand, each line read in a whisper before it is written. The first fake owes 1 line, the second 2, the third 4, since the nth fake owes 2 to the power of n minus 1 lines, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 lines and twenty fakes together owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because one scribe writes one line per breath at one tower and no copyist can write two scrolls at once, like one quill signing one name per dawn.
